title: Persistent ordered consumer for console metrics with backpressure and dedup
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Implement a durable, ordered consumer service for Console metrics that guarantees per-route ordering, supports flow-control/backpressure, and provides idempotent processing for downstream analytics. This ticket includes design, implementation, testing, rollout, and observability. The consumer will be the canonical ingress for route-level telemetry (token-level usage, request durations, model selection) and must be able to sustain spikes, recover quickly after restarts, and maintain schema compatibility as Console metrics evolve. We will prototype on NATS JetStream for its lightweight ordered streams and consumer ACK semantics, with an abstraction layer so we can switch to Kafka/Pulsar if requirements change.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route event ordering preserved end-to-end for 99.99% of events measured over a 24h window across 1M events
Consumer restart + rebalance complete and consuming again within 30s under undisturbed network conditions
Backpressure propagates: when downstream processor lag grows over 60s, producer throttling triggers and the system avoids unbounded memory growth
Idempotency: duplicate events (replayed or redelivered) must not create double-counts in aggregated metrics; unit/integration tests cover typical retry cases
End-to-end P95 latency from Console -> consumer -> processor <= 250ms for steady-state loads, documented in SLOs
Integration test against a JetStream testbench that simulates partition skew, replays, and node failures
Runbook and rollout plan in Confluence + canary with 5% traffic before full migration
Dashboard showing consumer lag, commit latency, ordering-violation rate, and percent of deduplicated events
PRs reviewed and merged with green CI and load test results attached (see links in notes)
